name: Sloth and Wasted Time

counsel.text: God would not have any live out of a calling: religion gives no warrant for idleness. It is a duty to labour six days, as well as keep holy rest on the seventh day.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the fourth commandment

counsel.text: Do you mortify; do you make it your daily work; be always at it whilst you live; cease not a day from this work; be killing sin or it will be killing you.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 2

counsel.text: When a man is weakened, made negligent or formal in duty, when he can omit duties or content himself with a careless, lifeless performance of them, without delight, joy, or satisfaction to his soul, who had another frame formerly; let him know, that though he may not be acquainted with the particular distemper wherein it consists, yet in something or other he is entered into temptation, which at the length he will find evident, to his trouble and peril.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: A Christian must not only mind heaven, but his calling. While the pilot has his eye to the star, he has his hand to the helm.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the fourth commandment

counsel.text: He that expects any thing from a man, applies himself to the ways and means whereby it may be obtained. The beggar that expects an alms lies at his door or in his way from whom he doth expect it. The way whereby and the means wherein Christ communicates himself is, and are, his ordinances ordinarily; he that expects any thing from him must attend upon him therein.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: If anything can make us rise off our bed of sloth, and serve God with all our might, it should be this, the hope of our near enjoyment of God for ever.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, man's chief end

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Father, I have wasted the time you gave me. I neglected my duties, put off what you set before me, and lost hours to idle things while your Word lay unopened and others needed me. I do not excuse it. Thank you that Christ was never idle in doing your will, and that his perfect obedience is counted as mine. His blood covers even this lost day. Forgive me for his sake. Holy Spirit, wake me up, make me hate this sloth, and give me a willing heart to serve you in my calling tomorrow. Amen.

prayers.title: To get up and go
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, I am sinking into idleness again. I feel heavy, and I do not want to move. You give strength to the weary, and you were never slow to do your Father's will. Give me enough strength for the next small duty in front of me. Help me put down this screen now and do my work as work done for you. Holy Spirit, stir up my heart and keep it warm toward you. Amen.

prayers.title: For the hours of this day
prayers.text: Father, my days are numbered, and this one will not come again. I have no need to be ruled by every distraction that calls to me. Turn my eyes away from what is empty, and give me a mind to use these hours well, in prayer, in work, in love to those around me, and in honest rest. Holy Spirit, make me faithful in small things today, for Christ's sake. Amen.

examinationQuestions: What were you avoiding today when you reached for your phone or put off your work?
Where did your heart go looking for rest today, to Christ or to amusement?
Which duties of your calling, at home, at work, at school, or in the church, did you neglect or do half-heartedly today?
How many hours went to screens and amusement today, and what did they give you in return?
Have you grown cold or careless in prayer, in the Word, or in worship, and when did that begin?
Are you resting in the ways God gives, such as sleep, the Lord's Day, and honest leisure, or only escaping?
fleeActions: Put your phone in another room, face down, and leave it there for the next hour.
Choose the one duty you have been putting off. Start it now and give it fifteen minutes.
Turn off the show or close the game, open your Bible, and read Proverbs 6:6-11.
Stand up, step outside or open a window, and pray as you walk.
Go and help someone in your home with a task, or call someone who needs a visit.
Ask a brother or sister in your church to check with you tomorrow on the work you mean to finish today.

afterFallReadings.text: Exercise and success are the two main cherishers of grace in the heart; when it is suffered to lie still, it withers and decays: the things of it are ready to die, Rev. 3:2; and sin gets ground towards the hardening of the heart, Heb. 3:13.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 2

afterFallReadings.text: Yea, let me add, that never any soul did or shall perish by the power of any lust, sin, or corruption, who could raise his soul by faith to an expectation of relief from Jesus Christ.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

afterFallReadings.text: I also saw, moreover, that it was not my good frame of heart that made my righteousness better, nor yet my bad frame that made my righteousness worse; for my righteousness was Jesus Christ Himself, the same yesterday, and to-day, and for ever (Heb. 13.8).
afterFallReadings.author: John Bunyan
afterFallReadings.source: Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners, §229
